p.src: Now Jia Zheng went to see the military governor and remained inside for half a day without emerging, while those waiting outside offered all manner of conjectures. Li Shi’er could learn nothing outside either. Remembering the famine reported in the gazette, he grew truly anxious. At last he heard that Jia Zheng had come out and hurried forward to follow him. Unable to wait until they returned, he seized a moment when no one was near and asked, “You were inside for so long, sir. Was there some urgent matter?” Jia Zheng smiled. “Nothing at all. It was only that the Commander-in-Chief of Zhenhai is related to His Excellency. He had written asking him to look after me, so His Excellency said a few kind words. He also said that we are related now ourselves.” Li Shi’er was delighted to hear this. His courage rising, he exerted himself all the more to urge Jia Zheng to consent to the marriage. Jia Zheng reflected that there might, after all, be some difficulty arising from Xue Pan’s affair. News reached him slowly out there, making it hard to take the necessary measures. Once back at his post, therefore, he sent a servant to the capital to make inquiries and, at the same time, report to Grandmother Jia that the Commander-in-Chief had proposed a marriage. If she approved, the Third Young Lady was to be brought to his place of office at once. Obeying his orders, the servant hastened to the capital and reported to Lady Wang. He then made inquiries at the Ministry of Personnel and learned that Jia Zheng had received no penalty; only the gentleman serving as acting magistrate of Taiping County had been dismissed. He immediately wrote a formal report to reassure Jia Zheng, then remained there awaiting a reply.

p.src: Meanwhile, in connection with the homicide case involving Xue Pan, Aunt Xue had spent untold sums of silver among the various government offices before the case was finally ruled an accidental killing and formally reported as such. She had originally intended to sell the pawnshop at a discount and use the proceeds to redeem him from punishment. Unexpectedly, the Ministry of Punishments returned the case for retrial. She engaged intermediaries and spent a great deal more money, but none of it did any good. He was still sentenced to death and kept in prison to await the great autumn assizes. Aunt Xue was both angry and heartsick, and wept day and night. Although Baochai often came over to console her, she would say, “Brother was ill-fated from the start. Having inherited all this property from our grandfather, he should have guarded it well and lived a steady, peaceful life. He had already caused disgraceful trouble in the south. The business with Xiangling alone was appalling enough: relying on the influence of our relatives and spending some silver, he got away with beating a young gentleman to death. After that, Brother should have mended his ways, become a decent man, and devoted himself to supporting Mother. Yet once he came to the capital, he carried on just as before. No one knows how much anger Mother has endured on his account, or how many tears she has shed. When a wife was found for him, the hope was that everyone might live together peacefully and comfortably. But fate would have it otherwise: the wife he married was restless and quarrelsome too, and that was why Brother fled the house. It was truly as the proverb says: ‘Enemies are bound to meet on a narrow road.’ Within a few days, it had led to a killing. No one can say that Mother and Second Brother failed to do everything in their power. Besides spending money, they humbled themselves before everyone and sought influence wherever they could. But there was no help for it: such was his fate, and he had only reaped what he had sown. People raise children so they will have someone to depend on in old age. Even a son from the poorest household earns enough for a bowl of rice to support his mother. Whoever heard of a son squandering a ready-made fortune and then making his aged mother weep herself half to death? I do not say this lightly, but with conduct like his, Brother is no son at all—he is an enemy sent to plague us. Yet Mother still will not see reason. She weeps from dawn till dusk and from dusk till dawn, while suffering Sister-in-law’s abuse besides. As for me, I cannot remain here constantly to comfort you. When I see Mother in this state, how can I possibly set my mind at rest? He may be foolish, but even he is unwilling to let me come back here. The other day, Master sent someone back to say that he had been terribly alarmed by what he saw in the capital gazette, and that was why he had sent a man to make arrangements. It seems to me that Brother’s mischief has caused a great many people anxiety. Fortunately, I am still nearby, almost as though I were at your side. If I had moved far from home and heard this news, I fear that longing and worrying for Mother would have driven me to my death. I beg Mother to compose herself for the time being. While Brother is still alive and able to answer questions, you should ask him about all the accounts. As for what others owe us and what we owe them, we should also call in one of the old clerks to settle the accounts and see whether any money remains.”

p.src: Aunt Xue said through her tears, “These past few days, whenever you came because of the trouble over your brother, either you comforted me or I told you what was happening at the yamen. But you still do not know that our name has already been struck from the register of official merchants in the capital, and two of our pawnshops have been turned over to others; the money we received for them has long since been spent. At another pawnshop, the manager absconded after leaving a deficit of several thousand taels, and that too has become entangled in the lawsuit. Your second brother is out collecting debts every day. By his reckoning, tens of thousands of taels have already been lost from the capital accounts, and only money from our share of the southern estate, together with the proceeds from selling the houses, will suffice to cover it. Two days ago I even heard a disturbing rumor that the family pawnshop in the south had also closed after losing its capital. If that is true, your mother will not be able to go on living.” With that, she burst into loud sobs again. Baochai, also weeping, tried to console her: “Mother, worrying about money will do no good. Second Brother is still here to manage matters for us. What is hateful is that those clerks, seeing our fortunes decline, were not content merely to go their separate ways; I have even heard that they are helping outsiders exploit us with false claims. It shows that, for all the years my brother has lived, everyone he befriended was no more than a fair-weather companion in wine and meat; not one of them is to be found in time of need. If you love me, Mother, then heed my words: you are no longer young, so please take good care of yourself. For the rest of your life, Mother, I do not think you will be reduced to freezing or starving. As for the few clothes and household things left here, we can only let Sister-in-law do as she pleases with them; nothing can be done about that. As for all the servants and old women, they plainly have no heart to remain here; let those who ought to leave go. Only poor Xiangling, who has suffered all her life, will have to come and live with you. If you truly lack anything and I have it, I can still bring some over; I am sure my husband would not object. Even Miss Xiren is upright and kindhearted; when she heard about my brother, she wept as soon as she mentioned you. My husband still thinks nothing is wrong, so he is not very anxious; if he heard, he too would be frightened half to death.” Before Baochai could finish, Aunt Xue said, “My dear girl, you must not tell him. He nearly lost his life over Miss Lin, and has only just begun to recover. If his distress brings on some illness or accident, not only will it add another burden to your troubles, but I shall be left with even less support.” “That was my thought too,” said Baochai, “so I have never told him.” As they spoke, they suddenly heard Jingui run into the outer room, wailing, “I no longer care whether I live or die! My husband has no chance of coming out of this alive.

p.src: So let us make a great uproar now and all go to the execution ground to fight it out!” As she spoke, she began wildly beating her head against the partition until her hair came loose and hung in disarray. Aunt Xue was so enraged that she could only stare with both eyes wide, unable to utter a word. Fortunately Baochai kept addressing her respectfully as “Sister-in-law” and coaxed her with every kind of gentle and stern persuasion. Jingui said, “Young Mistress, things are no longer as they were for you. You and your husband can live peacefully together, but I am all alone—what use have I for reputation?” With that, she made to rush into the street and return to her parents’ home. Fortunately there were many people present; they seized her and spent a long time persuading her before she finally quieted down. She frightened Baoqin so badly that Baoqin no longer dared appear before her. Whenever Xue Ke was at home, Jingui powdered and rouged her face, painted her brows and temples, and dressed herself in the most alluring and unusual fashion. She would repeatedly pass before his room, sometimes coughing deliberately, or, though she knew perfectly well he was inside, pointedly asking who was in the room. When she happened to meet Xue Ke, she would act coy and seductive, fussing over him with simpering affection, one moment delighted and the next petulant. Whenever the maids saw this, they hurried away to avoid her. She herself felt no shame, intent solely on stirring Xue Ke’s affections so that she might carry out her scheme involving Baochan. Xue Ke, however, did nothing but avoid her. When he occasionally encountered her, he dared not entirely refuse the courtesies, fearing that she would make a violent scene and turn malicious. Moreover, Jingui’s mind was clouded by lust: the more she looked at him, the more she loved him, and the more she thought of him, the deeper her fantasies became. How could she still distinguish whether Xue Ke’s attentions were genuine or feigned? There was only one thing: she saw that Xue Ke entrusted all his belongings to Xiangling’s care and that Xiangling also mended and washed his clothes. Whenever the two happened to be talking, they hurriedly separated as soon as Jingui arrived, which inflamed her jealousy still further. She wanted to vent her fury on Xue Ke, but could not bear to do so, and therefore laid all her hidden resentment upon Xiangling. Yet she feared that if she made trouble for Xiangling, she would offend Xue Ke; and so she was forced to swallow her resentment without revealing it.

p.src: One day, Baochan came over smiling and asked Jingui, “Mistress, have you seen Second Master?” “No,” said Jingui. Baochan laughed. “I knew Second Master’s show of prim propriety was not to be trusted. When we sent him wine the other day, he said he could not drink; but just now I saw him go into Madam’s room, his face flushed and reeking of liquor. If you do not believe me, Mistress, just wait for him by the gate to our courtyard. When he comes past from that direction, stop him and ask him yourself, and see what he says.” Jingui’s heart filled with anger when she heard this. “He will be coming out that way soon enough. Since he has no feeling or loyalty, why should I question him?” “You are being overly scrupulous again, Mistress,” said Baochan. If he answers pleasantly, we can do the same; if he does not, we can devise some other plan.” Jingui saw the sense in this and told Baochan to keep watch for him and see when he came out. Baochan assented and went outside. Jingui opened her dressing case, studied herself once more in the mirror, and touched up her lips. Then she took a flower-sprinkled silk handkerchief and was just about to go out when she seemed to remember something; suddenly, she had no idea what she ought to do. Just then she heard Baochan call outside, “You seem in fine spirits today, Second Master! Where have you been drinking?” Jingui knew perfectly well that this was a signal for her to come out, so she hurriedly raised the curtain and emerged. She saw Xue Ke telling Baochan, “Today is Master Zhang’s happy occasion. They pressed me so insistently that I had to drink half a cup, and my face is still burning even now.” Before he had finished, Jingui cut in: “Naturally, wine in other people’s homes tastes more delightful than wine in one’s own.” Stung by her insinuation, Xue Ke flushed still more deeply. He hurried over with an ingratiating smile and said, “How can you say such a thing, Sister-in-law?” Seeing the two of them begin to converse, Baochan slipped away into the room.

p.src: At first Jingui had meant only to feign anger and scold Xue Ke a little. But when she saw the faint flush on his cheeks, the bashfulness in his eyes, and the touching air of modest sincerity about him, all her haughty fierceness was instantly softened and banished to the ends of the earth. Smiling, she said, “So you mean they had to force you before you would drink?” “I have no head for wine at all,” said Xue Ke. “It is just as well that you do not drink,” said Jingui. “That is better than making trouble with drink as your brother does. When you marry your young mistress tomorrow, at least she will not be left lonely like me, a grass widow with a living husband!” As she said this, her eyes had already grown sidelong and seductive, and a blush had risen to both cheeks. Xue Ke found her words increasingly improper and made ready to leave. Jingui saw his intention, but she had no thought of letting him go. She had already stepped forward and seized him. Alarmed, Xue Ke cried, “Please conduct yourself with dignity, Sister-in-law!” As he spoke, his whole body trembled violently. Casting all shame aside, Jingui said, “Just come inside. I have something important to tell you.” In the midst of this commotion, someone suddenly called from behind them, “Mistress, Xiangling is coming!” Jingui jumped in fright. Turning, she saw that Baochan had raised the curtain to watch what was happening between them. When Baochan looked up and saw Xiangling approaching from the other direction, she had hurriedly warned Jingui. Jingui’s consternation was considerable, and her grip relaxed. Seizing the opportunity, Xue Ke broke free and ran away. Xiangling had been walking along without paying them any heed. Only when Baochan cried out did she notice Jingui gripping Xue Ke and desperately dragging him inside. Xiangling’s heart pounded with fright, and she hurriedly turned back. Meanwhile Jingui, shaken and furious, stood staring blankly after Xue Ke as he departed. She stood dazed for a long while, then gave an angry snort and returned to her room in bitter disappointment. From that day onward, she hated Xiangling to the marrow of her bones. Xiangling had in fact been on her way to Baoqin’s quarters. She had only just passed through the inner gate when she witnessed the scene and fled back in alarm.

p.src: That day, while Baochai was in Grandmother Jia's rooms, she heard Lady Wang tell the old lady about the proposed marriage for Tanchun. Grandmother Jia said, “If they are from the same province, that is very well. But I hear the young man has visited our house. Why did your master never mention it?” “Even we knew nothing of it,” replied Lady Wang. Grandmother Jia said, “It may be a good match, but the place is much too far away. Her father may be there now, but if he is transferred elsewhere in the future, will not our girl be left all alone?” Lady Wang said, “Since both families are in official service, no one can be certain where they will remain. Perhaps the other family will be transferred back here; and even if they are not, in the end fallen leaves return to their roots. Besides, since the master is serving there and his superior has already proposed the match, how could he well refuse it? I expect the master has already made up his mind, but did not wish to decide it on his own authority, and therefore sent someone to report the matter to you.” Grandmother Jia said, “If all of you approve, so much the better. But once Third Girl goes away, who knows whether she will be able to come home in two or three years? If it should be any longer, I fear I may not live to see her again.” As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes. Lady Wang said, “When girls grow up, sooner or later they must all be married into other families. Even if they marry someone from their own district, it is all very well if he holds no office; but if he is an official, who can guarantee that he will always remain in one place? All that matters is that the girls should be blessed with good fortune. Take Yingchun, for instance: she married quite nearby, yet we constantly hear that her husband beats and abuses her, and even denies her food. Even when we send things to her, they never reach her hands. Lately we hear that matters have grown still worse, and they will not even let her come home. Whenever the couple quarrel, he says that our family has spent his family's silver. The poor child can never look forward to a better day. The other day, worried about her, I sent someone to see her, but Yingchun hid in a side room and refused to come out. The old serving-women insisted on going in, and found our young lady wearing only a few old garments in such bitterly cold weather. Her eyes brimming with tears, she told them, ‘When you go back, do not tell them how wretched I am. This too is the fate I was born to. And there is no need to send me clothes or anything else: not only will they never reach me, but I shall merely earn another beating. They will say that I was the one who complained.’ Think of it, old lady: this is happening close by, where we can see it with our own eyes, and if things go badly, it only makes the suffering harder to bear. As things stand, Yingchun is truly worse off than even one of our third-rank serving-maids. Tanchun may not be my own child, but since the master has seen her prospective husband, he would certainly not have consented unless the young man were worthy. We need only ask you to give your instructions, choose an auspicious day, and send a good number of attendants to escort her to the master's place of office. u.src: That day, while Baochai was in Grandmother Jia's rooms, she heard Lady Wang tell the old lady about the proposed marriage for Tanchun.
Grandmother Jia said, “If they are from the same province, that is very well.
But I hear the young man has visited our house. Why did your master never mention it?”
“Even we knew nothing of it,” replied Lady Wang.
Grandmother Jia said, “It may be a good match, but the place is much too far away.
Her father may be there now, but if he is transferred elsewhere in the future, will not our girl be left all alone?”
Lady Wang said, “Since both families are in official service, no one can be certain where they will remain.
Perhaps the other family will be transferred back here; and even if they are not, in the end fallen leaves return to their roots.
Besides, since the master is serving there and his superior has already proposed the match, how could he well refuse it?
I expect the master has already made up his mind, but did not wish to decide it on his own authority, and therefore sent someone to report the matter to you.”
Grandmother Jia said, “If all of you approve, so much the better.
But once Third Girl goes away, who knows whether she will be able to come home in two or three years?
If it should be any longer, I fear I may not live to see her again.”
As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes.
Lady Wang said, “When girls grow up, sooner or later they must all be married into other families.
Even if they marry someone from their own district, it is all very well if he holds no office; but if he is an official, who can guarantee that he will always remain in one place?
All that matters is that the girls should be blessed with good fortune.
Take Yingchun, for instance: she married quite nearby, yet we constantly hear that her husband beats and abuses her, and even denies her food.
Even when we send things to her, they never reach her hands.
Lately we hear that matters have grown still worse, and they will not even let her come home.
Whenever the couple quarrel, he says that our family has spent his family's silver.
The poor child can never look forward to a better day.
The other day, worried about her, I sent someone to see her, but Yingchun hid in a side room and refused to come out.
The old serving-women insisted on going in, and found our young lady wearing only a few old garments in such bitterly cold weather.

Her eyes brimming with tears, she told them, ‘When you go back, do not tell them how wretched I am. This too is the fate I was born to. And there is no need to send me clothes or anything else: not only will they never reach me, but I shall merely earn another beating.
They will say that I was the one who complained.’
Think of it, old lady: this is happening close by, where we can see it with our own eyes, and if things go badly, it only makes the suffering harder to bear.
And as if that were not enough, the senior lady pays her no heed, while the senior master will not stand up for her!
As things stand, Yingchun is truly worse off than even one of our third-rank serving-maids.
Tanchun may not be my own child, but since the master has seen her prospective husband, he would certainly not have consented unless the young man were worthy.
We need only ask you to give your instructions, choose an auspicious day, and send a good number of attendants to escort her to the master's place of office.
Whatever arrangements are proper, the master will certainly not slight them.”

p.src: Grandmother Jia said, “Since her father has made the decision, see that everything is properly arranged, choose an auspicious day for a long journey, and send her off. That will settle the matter.” Lady Wang replied, “Yes.” Baochai had heard everything clearly, but dared not utter a word. Inwardly she lamented, “Of all the girls in our family, she is the finest; and now she too is to marry far away. Before our very eyes, the people here are dwindling away day by day.” When Lady Wang rose to take her leave, Baochai accompanied her out, then went straight back to her own room without saying a word to Baoyu. Finding Xiren working there alone, however, she told her what she had heard. Xiren too was deeply distressed.

p.src: Aunt Zhao, on the other hand, was delighted when she heard about Tanchun. She thought, “That girl of mine has always looked down on me at home. Though I am supposed to be her mother, I am treated worse than one of her maids. What is more, she always goes against the natural current to protect other people. With her standing in the way, even Huan'er can never get ahead. Now that the master is sending for her, I shall at least be rid of her. There is no hope of ever getting her to show me filial respect. I only hope she ends up like Yingchun; then I shall have my wish.” Thinking thus, she hurried over to Tanchun's quarters to congratulate her. “Young lady, you are soon to fly high. Once you are with your husband, you will naturally be better off than you are at home. I expect you are pleased with the arrangement yourself. Though I brought you into the world and raised you, I have never enjoyed the least benefit from you. Even if I have seven parts bad in me, I still have three parts good. Once you have gone, do not put me entirely out of your mind.” Finding her words utterly unreasonable, Tanchun merely lowered her head over her work and said nothing. Seeing that Tanchun paid no attention to her, Aunt Zhao went away by herself in a huff.

p.src: Meanwhile, Tanchun was at once angry, amused, and heartbroken, but she could do nothing except shed tears by herself. After sitting for a while, she went despondently to Baoyu's rooms. Baoyu asked her, “Third Sister, I heard that you were there when Cousin Lin died. I also heard that, when she died, music could be heard in the distance. Perhaps she truly came from some other realm.” Tanchun laughed. “You merely imagined it because that was what you had in mind. Still, that night was indeed strange: the sound was unlike the music played in ordinary households. So perhaps what you say is true.” Hearing this, Baoyu became all the more convinced that it was true. He recalled how, while his spirit had wandered the other day, he had seen someone who said that Daiyu had been unlike ordinary mortals in life and would be unlike ordinary ghosts in death; she must therefore have been a fairy who had descended to the human world. Then he suddenly remembered the actress who had played the Moon Goddess Chang'e that year—how ethereal and beautiful she had been, and how exquisite her bearing. After a while, Tanchun left. Baoyu insisted that Zijuan be brought to him, so Grandmother Jia was immediately informed and asked to send for her. Zijuan was reluctant at heart, but since Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang had ordered her to come, she had no choice. In Baoyu's presence, however, she did nothing but sigh and groan. In private, Baoyu would take hold of her and humbly question her about Daiyu, but Zijuan never gave him a civil answer. Baochai, for her part, privately praised Zijuan's loyalty and did not blame her. Although Xueyan had helped on the night of Baoyu's wedding, Baochai found her rather simple-minded. She therefore consulted Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, then married her to a young manservant so that the two might make a life of their own. Nanny Wang kept her in her care so that in due course she could escort Daiyu's coffin back south. Yingge and the other young maids continued to wait upon the Old Lady. Baoyu's thoughts had begun with Daiyu and then extended to those around her; when he reflected that all her attendants had already scattered like clouds, he grew more dejected still. When his misery became unbearable, he suddenly reflected that Daiyu's death had been so unmistakable that she must have left the mortal world and returned to the realm of immortals; at this thought, he became glad instead. Suddenly he heard Xiren and Baochai discussing Tanchun's marriage. With a cry of “Oh!” Baoyu collapsed weeping upon the kang. Startled, Baochai and Xiren hurried over to help him up, asking, “What is the matter?” Baoyu was already sobbing too hard to speak. After collecting himself for a while, he said, “Life has become unbearable! One after another, all my sisters are scattering! Cousin Lin has gone away to become an immortal. Eldest Sister is already dead. That at least can be borne, since she was not with us every day. Second Sister has fallen into the hands of an utterly vile scoundrel. Now Third Sister is to marry far away, and I shall never see her again. And no one knows where Cousin Shi will go. Cousin Xue is already promised in marriage. Must every one of these elder and younger sisters leave the family? What is the use of leaving me here all alone?”

p.src: Xiren hurriedly tried once more to console him. Baochai waved her hand. “Do not try to console him. Let me question him.” Then she asked Baoyu, “Would you, if you had your way, keep all these sisters at home to accompany you into old age, without any of them making provision for her own future? If they were unrelated to you, you might perhaps have some other intention. But these are your own sisters. Even if one of them were to marry far away—and there is no saying that any will—the Master would decide it. What could you possibly do? Do you imagine that you alone in all the world care for your sisters? If everyone behaved as you do, even I could not remain with you. People study books in order to understand reason. How is it that you grow more muddle-headed by the day? If that is how you feel, Miss Xiren and I had better each go our own way, and you can invite all your sisters here to keep watch over you.” Hearing this, Baoyu seized Baochai and Xiren each by one hand. “I understand all that too. But why must everyone scatter so soon? It would not be too late to part after I have turned to ashes.” Xiren covered his mouth with her hand. “There you go, talking nonsense again. You have only just begun to feel better these past two days, and Second Mistress has only just started eating again. If you make yourself ill again, I shall wash my hands of you.” As Baoyu gradually listened, he realized that both women spoke reasonably, yet he still did not know what to do with the feelings in his heart. He could only force himself to say, “I do understand, but my heart is in such turmoil.” Baochai ignored him and quietly told Xiren to give him a Calming-the-Heart Pill at once, then reason with him gently. Xiren was about to tell Tanchun that she need not come to say farewell before leaving, but Baochai said, “What is there to fear? Let a few peaceful days pass until his mind clears. Then we should let them speak together at greater length. Besides, Third Miss is an exceptionally sensible person, not one of those affected hypocrites. She is sure to offer him some earnest admonition. After that, he will not behave this way again.” While they were speaking, Grandmother Jia sent Yuanyang over to say that she had heard Baoyu's old illness had returned. She told Xiren to comfort and reassure him and keep him from indulging in wild thoughts. Xiren and the others assented. Yuanyang sat for a while, then left. Grandmother Jia then remembered Tanchun's impending journey. Though no bridal trousseau was to be prepared, all the articles she would need ought to be made ready. She therefore summoned Xifeng, explained the Master's intentions to her, and ordered her to see to the arrangements at once. Xifeng accepted the charge. How she managed the arrangements will be told in the next chapter.
